scholarships.title: Ireland Fellows Programme
scholarships.official_source: Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (Irish Aid), Government of Ireland

existing.description: The Ireland Fellows Programme offers people from around the world the opportunity to spend one year studying at Master's level in Ireland. It is fully funded by the Irish Government and offered under the auspices of the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, and is managed by the Embassy of Ireland responsible for each applicant's eligible country. The award covers programme fees, flights, accommodation and living costs for a one-year Master's placement running 10 to 16 months. Roughly 224 Fellowships were awarded for 2025/26 across 48 countries, with applications organised in three annual stages.
eligibility: National of a country eligible for the relevant strand (Africa, Kader Asmal for South Africa, Roger Casement for Nigeria, Seán McBride for Namibia, Archbishop Michael Courtney for Burundi, Frank Ferguson Fellowship in Engineering for Zambia, Asia, Latin America, or SIDS)
Early to mid-career professional with leadership potential
Admission to an eligible Master's level programme at an Irish higher education institution
IELTS certificate or equivalent, as required by Irish higher education institutions
All eligibility criteria for the chosen strand must be met
existing.eligibility_summary: Open to early to mid-career professionals from eligible developing countries with leadership potential who hold a relevant Bachelor's degree, applying to an eligible Master's programme in Ireland. Each strand has its own eligible countries and subject areas, and some strands are by invitation only.
benefits: Living costs for a one-year placement
Fully supported calendar of orientations, social and networking events, support and specialist training
requirements: Meet all eligibility criteria for the relevant strand
Secure an eligible Master's place at an Irish higher education institution
Apply only through the Embassy or channel named for your strand
Complete all three stages of the annual application process
documents: Stage 2 detailed application form with originals of all required documents
existing.english_requirement: IELTS certificate or equivalent is required by Irish higher education institutions; early preparation is strongly advised.
application_method: Stage 2 detailed application with original documents, on invitation from the Embassy
existing.selection_notes: Managed by the Embassy of Ireland responsible for the applicant's eligible country. Some strands are by invitation only from designated partner organisations, and unsolicited applications in those countries are not considered. The programme explicitly encourages applications from the broadest possible base and welcomes applicants with disabilities and applicants from minority or disadvantaged groups.
existing.best_fit: Early to mid-career professionals from eligible developing countries seeking a fully funded one-year Master's degree in Ireland with leadership and capacity-building focus.
existing.notes: One of Irish Aid's most longstanding programmes, running for over 50 years; almost 4,000 people have studied in Ireland through it. 224 Fellowships were awarded for 2025/26, representing 48 countries. Implementation in Ireland is supported by the Irish Council for International Students (ICOS). The separate Ireland–Palestine Scholarship Programme is a distinct award and should not be conflated with this one.
existing.duration: One year (10-16 months depending on the programme)
existing.application_period: Annual cycle: Stage 1 preliminary application approximately June/July, Stage 2 detailed application approximately mid-September to mid-October, Stage 3 interviews approximately November/December.
existing.deadline_display: "Applications for the 2027/28 academic year are now closed." The next cycle follows a recurring three-stage annual process: Stage 1 preliminary applications approximately June/July, Stage 2 detailed applications approximately mid-September to mid-October, Stage 3 interviews approximately November/December.
